::: {#exm-prior-predictive}
#### Prior predictive distribution of a count

In the Beta-Bernoulli model of @exm-beta-bernoulli,
the number of successes $R = \sumin Y_i$ given $\prob$ is $\operatorname{Binomial}(n, \prob)$.
Under the uniform $\dBetaf{1, 1}$ prior,
its prior predictive probabilities are

$$
\ba
\Prf{R = r}
&= \int_0^1 \binom{n}{r} \prob^{r} (1 - \prob)^{n - r} \cdot 1 \, d\prob
&& \text{(definition of the prior predictive distribution)}\\
&= \binom{n}{r} \frac{r!\,(n - r)!}{(n + 1)!}
&& \text{(the Beta integral)}\\
&= \frac{n!}{r!\,(n - r)!} \cdot \frac{r!\,(n - r)!}{(n + 1)!}
&& \text{(definition of the binomial coefficient)}\\
&= \frac{n!}{(n + 1)!}
&& \text{(the factor $r!\,(n - r)!$ appears above and below)}\\
&= \frac{1}{n + 1}
&& \text{($(n + 1)! = (n + 1) \cdot n!$)},
\ea
$$

for $r = 0, 1, \ldots, n$.
So the uniform prior says that, before seeing the data,
every count of successes is equally likely
[@gelman2013bda, Section 2.4, p. 34].
For the `r nrow(MASS::birthwt)` mothers in the `birthwt` data,
the code below computes these probabilities
from the Beta-binomial probability mass function:

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: prior-predictive-uniform
#| code-fold: false
n_mothers <- nrow(MASS::birthwt)
counts <- 0:n_mothers
prior_pred <- choose(n_mothers, counts) *
  beta(counts + 1, n_mothers - counts + 1) / beta(1, 1)
c(
  smallest = min(prior_pred),
  largest = max(prior_pred),
  one_over_n_plus_1 = 1 / (n_mothers + 1)
)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: prior-predictive-uniform-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

n_mothers = len(pd.read_csv("data/birthwt.csv"))
counts = np.arange(n_mothers + 1)
prior_pred = stats.betabinom.pmf(counts, n_mothers, 1, 1)
{
    "smallest": prior_pred.min(),
    "largest": prior_pred.max(),
    "one_over_n_plus_1": 1 / (n_mothers + 1),
}
```
